A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SkeletonLLM research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition, cross-format transfer, captioning, Motion-QA, ablation, and computational-efficiency results.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds joint-dataset training, external-MLLM comparisons, and a cross-format NFM visualization.

M1.justification: DrAction, LBS, NFM with GRU, the backbone, and the four-stage training procedure remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of blending weights, generative classification, and training losses largely restate v1's appendix details. Joint-dataset training and external-backbone tests do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use NTU-60/120, NTU-60 2D poses, NW-UCLA, HumanML3D, PKU-MMD, and Skeleton-QA for the same recognition, captioning, QA, and cross-format tasks. The added experiments combine existing datasets or change model configurations without extending data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 6 adds GPT-4o with fixed 3D+Velocity rendering, GPT-4o with DrAction, and GPT-5.4 with DrAction as recognition comparators. Existing comparator sets in the retained benchmark tables remain unchanged. GPT-4o's earlier role as a teacher was not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v4 adds joint NTU-60/HumanML3D training with shared DrAction and MLLM, plus external-MLLM evaluation on NTU-60 48/12 and 30/30. These supplement unchanged original splits, metrics, and training settings. The explicit identification of one checkpoint across tasks clarifies existing evaluations rather than establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v4 adds tests of joint-dataset compatibility and renderer transfer to external MLLMs, plus Figure 11's cross-format NFM color-modulation analysis. It removes v1 Appendix A.4/Table 8, which tested teacher label conditioning and retaining the final label in distillation targets. The broader component and sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix E.1 retains the same single-test-run statement. Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Rounding the Motion-QA scores does not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v4 adds joint-training results, including 88.52% NTU-60 accuracy and 65.04% NW-UCLA transfer accuracy, and external-MLLM results in Table 6. These are new configurations, not revisions to the original model's scores. It removes the CR-Distill variant results. Tables 1–3 retain their values; the Motion-QA changes are equivalent rounding, and Table 4 consolidates existing results.

T1.justification: The numbered mathematical formulations, rendering equations, SO(3) projection, and training objectives are retained. Formulas brought into the main text largely repeat existing appendix material; the finite-difference velocity expression supplies implementation detail rather than a new theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain format-agnostic differentiable rendering and cooperative training for universal skeleton understanding. The abstract foregrounds recognition while retaining captioning, QA, and cross-format capabilities; the introduction's contribution list and conclusion remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations about complementary learning across datasets, renderer transfer beyond the trained backbone, and NFM emphasizing corresponding body regions across formats. Figure 11 explicitly distinguishes RGB modification magnitude from classifier attention. The explanation supporting label-conditioned, full-response distillation is removed with its ablation; the existing applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: v4 specifies finite-difference velocity computation, the fixed 3D+Velocity baseline renderer and its settings, and checkpoint reuse across tasks. It replaces the promised future code release with a repository address for code and rendered videos. Most hardware, hyperparameters, architecture details, and prompt templates were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion and citations for UniMotion, SUGAR, FSAR, and heterogeneous skeleton representation learning, and clarifies the point-cloud context of Li et al. The overall positioning remains unchanged. TDSM's updated publication metadata identifies the same work.

P1.justification: v4 expands selected method explanations, revises the abstract and related-work passages, adds experimental discussion and acknowledgements, and removes Appendix A.4. These are localized edits within a largely retained narrative and section structure.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 4–6 and the NFM visualization in Figure 11, removes v1 Table 8, and adjusts captions and table presentation. Table 4 redisplays existing results. Most existing figures are reused, with relocation and repagination rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v4 improves methodological clarity and access information, explicitly establishes checkpoint reuse, and adds useful evidence on joint training and renderer transfer (Tables 4–6 and Figure 11). These gains are limited by the removal of the CR-Distill variant study and sparse procedural detail for the new experiments. The central method and original benchmark findings remain stable.
